LATIN PROSE FOR TRANSLATION
Each passage is followed by a close and faithful English rendering, sentence for sentence. English words between <<SEED>> and <</SEED>> are copied unchanged.

pairs.latin: Puer in agro ambulabat cum canem parvum vidit. Canis sub arbore iacebat et tremebat. Puer eum sustulit et domum portavit.
pairs.english: A boy was walking in the field when he saw a small dog. The dog was lying under a tree and trembling. The boy picked it up and carried it home.

pairs.latin: Mercator equum suum ad flumen duxit. Aqua alta et celeris erat, itaque ripam diu spectavit. Denique pontem petivit, quamquam longe aberat.
pairs.english: The merchant led his horse to the river. The water was deep and swift, so he looked at the bank for a long time. At last he made for the bridge, although it was far away.

pairs.latin: Soror mea epistulam e Roma accepit. Eam legit, deinde ridens mihi dedit. "Pater noster," inquit, "mox revertetur."
pairs.english: My sister received a letter from Rome. She read it, then gave it to me with a smile. "Our father," she said, "will soon return."

pairs.latin: Nauta ad portum rediit. <<SEED>>"Not a word," he told the boy.<</SEED>> Deinde navem reliquit et in tabernam intravit.
pairs.english: The sailor came back to the harbour. <<SEED>>"Not a word," he told the boy.<</SEED>> Then he left the ship and went into the inn.
